outcome: proportion of infants with low CHr (<29 pg)
cohort: The study included 315 very low birth weight (VLBW) infants from two tertiary level Neonatal Intensive Care Units.
finding: Approximately 31.4% of very low birth weight infants had low reticulocyte hemoglobin content (CHr) prior to discharge, indicating iron deficiency, and delayed cord clamping improved hematological parameters and reduced the incidence of low CHr in this population.
